core.title: Every internal cross-reference in the documentation corpus resolves
core.given: The documentation corpus is being validated, whatever changed.
core.when: The documentation validator checks the corpus's internal cross-references between corpus documents.
core.then: Every internal cross-reference MUST resolve. An unresolvable internal reference is FAIL.
prefer: Fix a reported reference by fixing its target or the reference itself
avoid: Leaving an internal cross-reference that points at a document or anchor that does not exist
unless: External links are not resolved. Their liveness is a network property, and checking it would make the gate non-deterministic.
core.why: Unresolvable internal references must be VALIDATION FAILURES: a documentation corpus whose internal references dangle is not a passing corpus.
evidence: The documentation validation report lists no unresolved internal reference
verification: Scope: the check resolves internal cross-references — references from one document in the corpus to another document or anchor in it — where the constructs that count as an internal cross-reference come from the stack profile. External links are out of scope, because their liveness is a network property, not a corpus property.
If the render could not run (absent toolchain, or a failure not attributable to a document), reference resolution was not observed. The verdict is COULD_NOT_CHECK: never PASS and never FAIL.
Severity 1. Disposition strict: fails on every finding; no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.

Activation is every validation of the configured documentation corpus, whatever changed and whatever the result. The core assumes no corpus directory, file kind or extension; no finding gates activation (an unresolved-reference finding sets the verdict to FAIL, it does not change whether the rule fires); and generated render output is never an input — the exact never-scanned trees are the stack's single exclusion list (roots.excluded).

fires: Every validation of the documentation corpus, including a clean one
A plan artifact or a corpus document adds an internal cross-reference that points at another corpus document
A document or anchor is renamed, moved or deleted while other documents still reference it
doesNotFire: Checking whether external (http/https) link targets are live. The document that contains them must still render, and its internal references must still resolve.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete markup constructs by which one document in the documentation corpus cross-references another document or an anchor within it; these are the references the validator must resolve.
Generated render output is never an input to the documentation check; the exact never-scanned trees come from the stack's single exclusion list.

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself is fully stack-neutral. Only two facts are stack data, both carried by the profile: the cross-reference syntax (proposed as idiom.docs_syntax#internal_reference; no existing key covers intra-corpus cross-reference constructs) and the excluded render-output tree (docs/dist/**, supplied via roots.excluded, with the core deferring the exact list to the stack's single exclusion list). The asciidoctor-vs-Python-renderer rationale, the concrete .adoc xref example, and the validator id docs_capability remain bunOnly. 'docs_validation' (phase), the verdict vocabulary (PASS/FAIL/COULD_NOT_CHECK), 'render' and 'toolchain' are treated as harness-level terms, neutral across stacks; http/https in doesNotFire is a universal URL scheme, not a stack artifact, so it was kept.
